newsitem.title: UK: UK parliamentary business to end on Friday.
newsitem.headline: UK parliamentary business to end on Friday.

text.p: The Building Societies bill is one of more than two dozen measures whose legislative fate was in the balance on Monday, after Prime Minister John Major announced that parliament would be prorogued this Friday.
Although parliament will not be formally dissolved until April 8, all unfinished business will be ended with the prorogation ceremony on Friday, government officials said.

Tony Newton, leader of the House of Commons, said government and opposition business managers were meeting to agree how to deal with the significant number of bills currently before both houses of parliament.
Newton told the House of Commons that he hoped to make a more substantive statement later in the day on what remaining business would be handled.
The Building Socities bill is a possible casualty of the logjam, even though it enjoys cross-party support.
"One must now be somewhat doubtful that this bill can really make progress," Labour MP Peter Pike said as the Commons opened line-by-line scrutiny of the measure.
